territories.name: Room Beacon
territories.thesis: Turn the phone into a shared stage prop: the visible group reads and debates a giant game claim while the holder performs one unmistakable group commit.
territories.audienceFit: Fits a friend group seeking fast, performative shared play without requiring profiles, private devices, or social-feed literacy.
territories.taskFit: Optimizes forehead play, distance reading, and rematch tempo while retaining a tap fallback with the same answer and group-score semantics.
territories.contentStructure: An active game board carries only game context, statement, attribution, time, and readiness; review becomes a structurally distinct truth panel with explanation, source status, and reporting.

structure.hierarchy: Statement dominates; attribution, game context, timer, and commit readiness follow in that order.
structure.navigationModel: One forward social loop with an adjacent review queue and a retained-session rematch action.
structure.interactionModel: Forehead tilt is the signature commit, backed by an equally scored blind tap path and explicit sensor recovery.

axes.typography: large condensed display face with plain utility labels
axes.density: very low density during active play
axes.geometry: hard rectangular perimeter and directional bands
axes.color: high-contrast energetic fields without pre-reveal truth mapping
axes.imagery: no portraits; typographic signal and abstract light only
axes.signature: persistent perimeter game beacon that also communicates neutral, ready, committed, and recovery states

risks: The beacon may be cropped from captured claims.
Long statements may undermine the stage-like hierarchy.
Spectacle may overstate motion value before accessible evidence exists.

assumptionDependencies.rationale: The territory makes group-visible forehead play the primary social ritual and must earn its extra control complexity.
Explicit role rehearsal tests whether a room-scale board removes moderator explanation rather than adding spectacle.
Truth is deliberately deferred to the common review contract rather than proven by the active board.
The territory depends on several-feet group reading of realistic statement and attribution lengths.
Blind tap, non-motion, and screen-reader role scripts must retain the same group outcome without leaking the card.
The common fixture, not the stage treatment, supplies approved representative content.
The perimeter marker must remain game context in normal crops without exposing authenticity.

criterionEvaluations.rationale: The role rehearsal is plausible but requires group sessions without moderator explanation.
Large active type helps, but maximum-length cards and distance conditions may collapse the sparse hierarchy.
Tilt remains prominent, so duplicate-commit and sensor-recovery evidence is essential.
The distinct review panel can clarify truth only if captured pre-reveal states remain clearly game-owned.
The holder cannot see the board; equivalent blind controls and role-specific audio behavior must be tested.
A single forward room loop and retained-session rematch directly support fast group continuation.
A shared claim board and holder commit are specific to this one-phone authenticity ritual, not a feed.
The perimeter state language must cover sensor, offline, interruption, and tombstone recovery without becoming decorative.
Readable landscape posture, motion handling, and orientation recovery require native device validation.
Review panels must contain every canonical truth state without special cases.
The territory uses no identity, source, or sensor data on active play beyond the shared reporting contract.

territories.name: Tabletop Deck
territories.thesis: Make every round an authored game object whose question face and truth back perform visibly different jobs: playful ambiguity first, accountable explanation after.
territories.audienceFit: Fits groups familiar with physical party games who want a tangible shared object without mistaking it for a public post or a fact-check product.
territories.taskFit: Balances forehead, tap, and pass-and-play by using the same card semantics across formats and making review a deliberate collective choice.
territories.contentStructure: A clearly marked game claim face contains the active prompt; a separate truth back begins with the explicit classification, then explanation, allowed source status, report, and next action.

structure.hierarchy: Question face prioritizes game context and claim; truth back prioritizes full classification before result and evidence.
structure.navigationModel: A seeded deck sequence leads to an ordered review stack that preserves place after source and report actions.
structure.interactionModel: Tilt and large labeled taps are equal commits; a semantic face replacement replaces any card-turn motion under Reduce Motion.

axes.typography: expressive editorial display with monospaced evidence labels
axes.density: medium density with a sparse question face and denser review back
axes.geometry: layered rectangular card stack and printed edge treatments
axes.color: restrained deck-specific patterns with truth expressed in words and shapes
axes.imagery: abstract printed textures only; no posts, screenshots, or public-figure photos
axes.signature: front-to-back claim object that becomes an explicit truth record after the round

risks: A quote card may look authoritative when photographed.
The truth back may slow rematch tempo.
Evidence labels may drift toward newsroom or verification-badge cues.

assumptionDependencies.rationale: The same card semantics work in forehead and private formats without assuming one is preferred.
The face distinction must explain guess-now versus verify-later without an instruction-heavy lobby.
The territory tests whether an explicit truth back and explanation actually restore trust after intentional pre-answer ambiguity.
The centered card must hold realistic maximum content without shrinking attribution or context.
Semantic replacement and equal taps are designed into the shared access contract but still require participant evidence.
Every review back must express authentic, fabricated, disputed, unavailable, and removed semantics from real editorial records.
The game-context phrase must survive a reasonable crop of the question face without leaking truth status.

criterionEvaluations.rationale: The question/truth distinction needs unaided group comprehension evidence.
A bounded card can constrain maximum-length copy at party distance.
Large labeled taps and semantic state replacement provide a clear non-motion path.
A truth back beginning with a full classification directly serves post-answer explanation.
VoiceOver, TalkBack, and private handoff order must be tested with regular users.
A deliberate review stack may compete with immediate rematch momentum.
Game claim and truth back avoid feed and news authority while centering the product's transition.
Nonplayable states and queued reports must be intelligible without treating them as cards to answer.
The bounded structure can use native semantic replacement rather than complex visual motion.
Source and removal semantics must not force a one-off back-face design for every exception.
The review object exposes only allowed explanation and report actions; payload policy stays shared.

territories.name: Private Relay
territories.thesis: Challenge forehead primacy with a tap-first, role-explicit relay in which predictable control, protected handoff, and accessible private judgment create the social confidence.
territories.audienceFit: Fits mixed-ability groups and pass-and-play sessions that value clear ownership, privacy, and low-friction continuation over theatrical motion.
territories.taskFit: Makes the active actor, private answer, score ownership, and next-player handoff explicit while retaining forehead play as an equivalent optional format.
territories.contentStructure: A persistent role strip frames private prompt, timer, and labeled verdict controls; a protected shutter precedes every handoff, interruption recovery, and next-player reveal.

structure.hierarchy: Current role and game context precede statement, attribution, timer, controls, then the protected next action.
structure.navigationModel: Turn-by-turn relay with a privacy checkpoint between players and a calm review sheet after outcomes.
structure.interactionModel: Labeled taps are primary; extended and untimed choices occur before the round; forehead tilt remains available without changing score semantics.

axes.typography: high-legibility humanist system with tabular timing
axes.composition: portrait stacked relay panels with a persistent role strip
axes.density: moderate functional density with explicit state labels
axes.geometry: flat bounded zones and privacy shutter rules
axes.color: quiet neutral base with one interaction accent and text-plus-shape meaning
axes.imagery: no decorative imagery; state and role language provide identity
axes.signature: role ribbon and protected privacy shutter across handoff, interruption, and recovery

risks: The utility-forward surface may resemble generic trivia.
Tap-first play may lose the social value that justifies forehead mode.
Role labels may add setup clutter.

assumptionDependencies.rationale: The countermodel tests whether tap-first private relay can retain enough social value to displace forehead primacy.
Explicit current-role labels must simplify, rather than lengthen, first-round understanding.
The common calm review sheet carries truth semantics independently of the active relay design.
Private portrait play reduces group-distance dependence but forehead mode still uses the shared fixture conditions.
The territory's value depends on accessible, role-appropriate completion without hidden degraded paths.
Editorial card quality remains shared across formats and is not established by relay structure.
The role strip and game context must remain in capture while private prompts disclose no authenticity outcome.

criterionEvaluations.rationale: Persistent role ownership and a protected next action directly expose who does what first.
Portrait private play may not provide an equally compelling screen-facing group experience in forehead mode.
Labeled taps, pre-round timer choices, and shuttered recovery reduce motion ambiguity.
A calm review sheet still needs testing for explicit fabricated and nonplayable state understanding.
Role-specific VoiceOver, TalkBack, no-motion, and protected handoff paths are central rather than fallback features.
Privacy checkpoints may slow a lively group even as they prevent spoilers.
Without the room spectacle, the relay may feel like ordinary private trivia.
The shutter and role strip are designed to explain interruption, handoff, and recovery without prior-card leakage.
Predictable native controls and focus restoration are more feasible than gesture-only dependence.
Review, report, and nonplayable records must be pressure-tested with the shared editorial fixture.
Private relay retains local role state without adding identity, transcript, or sensor collection.
